MUJAHID:v1p334#2/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p334#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p334#2/r1.claim: Mujahid says the drink of pus means pus and blood.

MUQATIL:14:13-16/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:14:13-16/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:14:13-16/r5.claim: Hell awaits the arrogant after death, where the wretched drink pus and blood from the bodies of unbelievers.

MAJAZ:v1p337/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p337/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p337/r1.claim: Min warāʾihi Jahannam means Hell is before him; Arabic may say death is behind you while meaning it lies ahead.

MAJAZ:v1p337/r2.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p337/r2.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p337/r2.claim: An anonymous poem uses warāʾ to mean before the Banū Riyāḥ, with them between speaker and addressee.

MAJAZ:v1p337/r3.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p337/r3.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p337/r3.claim: A second anonymous poem uses warāya for ahead of the speaker.

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p341#4/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p341#4/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p341#4/r1.claim: Qatada describes the drink of pus as fluid that runs between the skin and flesh.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p231#2/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p231#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p231#2/r1.claim: Min warāʾihi means ahead of him.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p231#2/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p231#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p231#2/r2.claim: Ṣadīd is pus and blood; one reading says his water becomes pus, while another compares the drink to pus.

TAB-FULL:v13p619/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p619/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p619/r1.claim: Ṣadīd is pus and blood; the word is grammatically an explanatory apposition to ماء.

TAB-FULL:v13p619/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p619/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v13p619/r2.claim: Mujahid glosses ṣadīd as pus and blood.

TAB-FULL:v13p619/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p619/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v13p619/r3.claim: Qatada describes ṣadīd as fluid flowing from the sinner’s blood, flesh, and skin.

TAB-FULL:v13p619/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p619/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v13p619/r4.claim: A further wording from Qatada describes it as what flows between the flesh and skin.

TAB-FULL:v13p619/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p619/r5.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v13p619/r5.claim: Al-Dahhak says it comes from the unbeliever’s interior, mixed with pus and blood.

ZAJJAJ:v3p156/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p156/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p156/r3.claim: Waraʾahu means before him here; it denotes what is hidden or out of sight, so it is not an opposite with both front and back meanings as some claim.

ZAJJAJ:v3p156/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p156/r4.speaker: النابغة
ZAJJAJ:v3p156/r4.claim: Al-Nābigha’s line uses warāʾ for what lies beyond: beyond God there is no other destination for a person.

ZAJJAJ:v3p156/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p156/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p156/r5.claim: Ṣadīd is fluid made of the blood and pus draining from Hell’s inhabitants.

THALABI:v5p308/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p308/r10.speaker: ابن كيسان
THALABI:v5p308/r10.claim: Ibn Kaysan describes the person as proudly defiant toward truth.

THALABI:v5p308/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p308/r11.speaker: ابن زيد
THALABI:v5p308/r11.claim: Ibn Zayd says عنيد means opposing the truth.

THALABI:v5p308/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p308/r12.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p308/r12.claim: In Arabic, the stubborn camel leaves the path; أهل المعاني say عنيد is one who confronts another in opposition, from عند meaning a side.

THALABI:v5p308/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p308/r13.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p308/r13.claim: An Arabic poem uses العند for the side or obstruction one cannot bear.

THALABI:v5p308/r14.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p308/r14.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p308/r14.claim: من ورائه can mean in front of him, as in death lying ahead; the same usage appears in the verse about a king behind the travelers.

THALABI:v5p308/r15.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p308/r15.speaker: أبو عبيدة
THALABI:v5p308/r15.claim: Abu Ubayda calls وراء a word with opposite meanings.

THALABI:v5p308/r16.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p308/r16.speaker: الأخفش
THALABI:v5p308/r16.claim: Al-Akhfash says وراء can mean something yet to come, as when someone says the other will come behind you.

THALABI:v5p308/r17.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p308/r17.speaker: مقاتل
THALABI:v5p308/r17.claim: Muqatil instead says Hell lies after the person.

THALABI:v5p308/r18.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p308/r18.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p308/r18.claim: صديد is pus and blood; Qatada says it is what comes out between the disbeliever's skin and flesh.

THALABI:v5p308/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p308/r5.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v5p308/r5.claim: Mujahid glosses عنيد as one who opposes and turns away from truth.

THALABI:v5p308/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p308/r6.speaker: إبراهيم
THALABI:v5p308/r6.claim: Ibrahim defines عنيد as one who veers away from the truth.

THALABI:v5p308/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p308/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v5p308/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas says عنيد means turning away.

THALABI:v5p308/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p308/r8.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v5p308/r8.claim: Qatada defines the stubborn rejecter as one who will not say there is no god but God.

THALABI:v5p310/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p310/r1.speaker: محمد بن كعب
THALABI:v5p310/r1.claim: Muhammad ibn Kab and al-Rabi ibn Anas identify صديد as the drainage of Hell's inhabitants.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p126/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p126/r13.speaker: أبو عبيدة
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p126/r13.claim: من ورائه جهنم may mean that Hell is behind him; أبو عبيدة notes that وراء can be an opposite, applying to what is behind or ahead.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p126/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p126/r14.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p126/r14.claim: Alternatively, Hell is ahead of him, as a cited poem uses وراء for what lies before someone.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p126/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p126/r15.speaker: ابن الأنباري
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p126/r15.claim: Hell may be behind him because it is hidden and cannot be seen.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p126/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p126/r16.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p126/r16.claim: من ورائه may mean that Hell comes after his death, supported by the Nabigha's line that there is no destination after God.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p128/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p128/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p128/r1.claim: صديد may mean a liquid like pus, by analogy with calling a brave man a lion to mean lion-like.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p128/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p128/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p128/r2.claim: Alternatively, صديد may derive from repulsion: water that the drinker finds repellent and turns away from.

QUSHAYRI:v2p119/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p119/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p119/r4.claim: The word behind can refer to what lies ahead or behind, since it means what is concealed; the verse can describe both future punishment and consequences of past evil.

QUSHAYRI:v2p119/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p119/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p119/r5.claim: The damned drink the foul liquid a sip at a time because its bitterness makes it impossible to swallow all at once.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p429/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p429/r1.speaker: ابن عباس والمفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p429/r1.claim: They take waraʾ as what lies ahead of the man: Hell is in front of him.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p429/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p429/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p429/r2.claim: Waraʾ can mean behind or ahead because its basic sense is what is concealed from someone; unseen ahead can be described like unseen behind.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p429/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p429/r3.speaker: أبو عبيدة وابن السكيت وأبو الهيثم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p429/r3.claim: They treat waraʾ as a word with opposite senses, meaning either behind or ahead.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p429/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p429/r4.speaker: أهل المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p429/r4.claim: Any place can be behind or ahead from a viewpoint, so waraʾ may mean ahead; the verse about a king ahead of travelers illustrates it.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p429/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p429/r5.speaker: ابن الأنباري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p429/r5.claim: He gives a third sense, after: Hell follows the despair implied by the preceding statement, like the poet's claim that none has a destination after God.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p429/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p429/r6.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p429/r6.claim: He reads waraʾ as after: Hell will catch up with the condemned, as severe cold behind someone will reach him; Labid uses the word for old age that will come upon him.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p432/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p432/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p432/r1.claim: Ṣadīd is the liquid from a wound, mixed with blood and pus.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p432/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p432/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p432/r2.claim: He identifies the drink as pus and blood issuing from adulterers private parts; al-Qurazi and al-Rabi share this view.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p432/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p432/r3.speaker: قتادة والكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p432/r3.claim: They say the liquid comes from the unbeliever skin and flesh.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p432/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p432/r4.speaker: أبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p432/r4.claim: He construes the phrase as water possessing pus; the author says this conflicts with the description of the drink given to the righteous.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:14:16-18/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:14:16-18/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:14:16-18/r1.claim: Hell lies ahead of the unbeliever, and the drink is pus flowing from a wound mixed with blood.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p340#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p340#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p340#2/r1.claim: Waraʾahu can mean ahead of him, as in the account of the king before the travelers.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p340#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p340#2/r2.speaker: أبو عبيدة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p340#2/r2.claim: Waraʾ is a word with opposite meanings.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p340#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p340#2/r3.speaker: الأخفش
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p340#2/r3.claim: Waraʾ may describe something that will come to you, or someone behind whom you will reach a destination.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p340#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p340#2/r4.speaker: مقاتل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p340#2/r4.claim: He takes Hell behind the condemned person, that is, after him.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p340#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p340#2/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p340#2/r5.claim: Ṣadīd is pus and blood flowing from the bodies of the unbelievers.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p340#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p340#2/r6.speaker: محمد بن كعب
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p340#2/r6.claim: He says the drink is what flows from adulterers' genitals and is given to the unbeliever.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p512#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p512#2/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p512#2/r4.claim: Min warāʾihi means before him; the author cites a verse using warāʾ for what lies ahead as evidence.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p512#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p512#2/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p512#2/r5.claim: Hell may be ahead of the damned in worldly life as they await it, or in the afterlife as they are raised and brought to it.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p512#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p512#2/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p512#2/r6.claim: The clause about being given pus coordinates with an omitted description of what happens in Hell, singling out one of its severest torments.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p512#2/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p512#2/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p512#2/r7.claim: Ṣadīd is an explanatory apposition to water, clarifying that it is fluid draining from the skin of Hell's inhabitants.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p331/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p331/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p331/r1.claim: The liquid is not actually water, but is called water because it takes water’s place; ṣadīd means pus and blood flowing from the people of Hell.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p331/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p331/r2.speaker: مجاهد والضحاك
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p331/r2.claim: Mujahid and al-Dahhak gloss ṣadīd as pus and blood.

TABRISI:14:13-18/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:14:13-18/r10.speaker: أبو عبد الله ع
TABRISI:14:13-18/r10.claim: The drink is the blood and pus flowing from the private parts of adulterers in Hell; most commentators share this interpretation.

TABRISI:14:13-18/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:14:13-18/r11.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:14:13-18/r11.claim: Alternatively, it looks like water but has the color and taste of pus.

TABRISI:14:13-18/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:14:13-18/r12.speaker: أبو أمامة
TABRISI:14:13-18/r12.claim: The Prophet says that the drink scorches the face and makes the scalp fall when brought near, then cuts through the drinker’s intestines; the report links this punishment to 47:15 and 18:29.

TABRISI:14:13-18/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:14:13-18/r13.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TABRISI:14:13-18/r13.claim: A wine drinker’s prayer is not accepted for forty days; if he dies with wine inside him, God gives him the pus of Hell’s people, including the gathered emissions of adulterers, which melts his insides and skin.

TABRISI:14:13-18/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:14:13-18/r8.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:14:13-18/r8.claim: Hell is before the tyrant, waiting ahead of him along with his loss.

TABRISI:14:13-18/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:14:13-18/r9.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:14:13-18/r9.claim: Alternatively, Hell is behind him; future time can be called ‘behind’ because it comes and overtakes a person from behind.

TABRISI:14:17-18/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:14:17-18/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TABRISI:14:17-18/r1.claim: The source identifies the transmitters of the preceding wine-and-Hell report as Shuʿayb ibn Wāqid, al-Ḥusayn ibn Zayd, al-Ṣādiq, and his forefathers.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p351#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p351#3/r1.speaker: ابن عباس وأبو عبيدة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p351#3/r1.claim: One interpretation of “behind him is Hell” is that Hell is ahead of him; Ibn Abbas and Abu Ubayda support this sense.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p351#3/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p351#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p351#3/r2.claim: A poem about the Marwanids uses warāʾ for what lies ahead, supporting the “in front” sense.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p351#3/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p351#3/r3.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p351#3/r3.claim: Another interpretation is “after,” specifically after he has despaired; the preceding “failed” implies despair.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p351#3/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p351#3/r4.speaker: النابغة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p351#3/r4.claim: Al-Nabigha's verse uses warāʾ to mean “after God,” supporting the second interpretation.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p351#3/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p351#3/r5.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p351#3/r5.claim: Al-Zajjaj says warāʾ means what is hidden from sight, whether in front or behind; he rejects treating it as a true antonym.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p351#3/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p351#3/r6.speaker: ثعلب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p351#3/r6.claim: Thaʿlab explains that warāʾ names what is hidden from one's sight, whether ahead or behind.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p351#3/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p351#3/r7.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p351#3/r7.claim: Al-Farra allows the forward sense for times and eras, but not to describe a person who is visibly in front or behind you.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p351#3/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p351#3/r8.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p351#3/r8.claim: “After God there is no destination” is the sense of the cited line, linking the verse's “behind” with what comes after.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p352/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p352/r1.speaker: عكرمة ومجاهد واللغويون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p352/r1.claim: Ikrima, Mujahid, and linguists define ṣadīd as pus.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p352/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p352/r2.speaker: قتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p352/r2.claim: Qatada says it is pus and blood coming out from between the disbeliever's skin and flesh.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p352/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p352/r3.speaker: القرظي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p352/r3.claim: Al-Qurazi identifies it as the drainage of Hell's inhabitants, flowing from adulterers' genitals.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p352/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p352/r4.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p352/r4.claim: Ibn Qutayba says ṣadīd is served in place of water, or that the water is likened to pus.

RAZI-FULL:v19p81/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p81/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p81/r1.claim: Warāʾ can name what is hidden from someone, whether in front or behind, as the cited verse and poetry show.

RAZI-FULL:v19p81/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p81/r2.speaker: أبو عبيدة وابن السكيت
RAZI-FULL:v19p81/r2.claim: Abu Ubayda and Ibn al-Sikkit say warāʾ is an antonymic word for both behind and in front; what is behind can turn into what is in front.

RAZI-FULL:v19p81/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p81/r3.speaker: ابن الأنباري
RAZI-FULL:v19p81/r3.claim: Ibn al-Anbari says warāʾ means after, as in the cited line that a person has no destination after God.

RAZI-FULL:v19p81/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p81/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p81/r4.claim: In context, the disbeliever's defeat comes first, and afterward he enters Hell.

RAZI-FULL:v19p81/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p81/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p81/r5.claim: The drinking clause coordinates with an understood phrase: he is cast into Hell and given pus to drink.

RAZI-FULL:v19p81/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p81/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p81/r6.claim: This drink is singled out because it seems among the severest forms of punishment, alongside near-death from every side without dying.

RAZI-FULL:v19p81/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p81/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p81/r7.claim: Ṣadīd may explain the water as the discharge flowing from the skins of Hell's inhabitants, or as water like pus that God creates in its stench, thickness, and filth.

RAZI-FULL:v19p81/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p81/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p81/r8.claim: Another explanation is that it is actual pus, so repulsive that its foulness prevents the drinker from taking it.

RAZI-FULL:v19p81/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p81/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p81/r9.claim: The image is linked to boiling water that cuts the bowels in Q 47:15 and molten water that scalds faces in Q 18:29.

QURTUBI-FULL:14:16-17/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:16-17/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:14:16-17/r1.claim: Waraʾahu Jahannam means Hell is after the unbeliever's destruction; waraʾ can mean after, as in al-Nābigha's line that no destination lies after God.

QURTUBI-FULL:14:16-17/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:16-17/r3.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:14:16-17/r3.claim: Waraʾ may instead mean in front of, supported by several poems and by the description of the king ahead of the people in 18:79; Abū ʿUbayda and Quṭrub adopt this sense.

QURTUBI-FULL:14:16-17/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:16-17/r4.speaker: الأخفش
QURTUBI-FULL:14:16-17/r4.claim: Al-Akhfash explains the word through idioms: something behind you will come to you, and being behind someone means pursuing him.

QURTUBI-FULL:14:16-17/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:16-17/r5.speaker: النحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:14:16-17/r5.claim: Al-Naḥḥās says waraʾahu means in front of him, not as a true antonym, but because what is hidden is concealed from view.

QURTUBI-FULL:14:16-17/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:16-17/r6.speaker: الأزهري
QURTUBI-FULL:14:16-17/r6.claim: Al-Azharī and also Abū ʿUbayda treat waraʾ as an antonym meaning either behind or in front, both rooted in concealment; Ibn al-Anbārī's explanation that Hell is hidden is judged good.

QURTUBI-FULL:14:16-17/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:16-17/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:14:16-17/r7.claim: Ṣadīd is water like pus by simile, or the pus and blood flowing from the people of Hell; Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb and al-Rabīʿ say it is their wash water from adulterers' genitals, while another view derives it from repelling a loathed drink.

BAYDAWI-FULL:14:16/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:16/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:16/r1.claim: Jahannam is ahead of the denier: he stands by its brink in this life and is sent to it in the next.

BAYDAWI-FULL:14:16/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:16/r2.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:16/r2.claim: Another reading of behind is what comes after his life; its basic sense is what is concealed from view.

BAYDAWI-FULL:14:16/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:16/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:16/r3.claim: The clause about being given water is coordinated with an omitted clause describing what is done to him in Hell.

BAYDAWI-FULL:14:16/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:16/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:16/r4.claim: Ṣadīd is an explanatory apposition for water: fluid that runs from the skin of Hell's inhabitants.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p226#5/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p226#5/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p226#5/r1.claim: Waraʾ means ahead: Hell may be described as ahead of him in this life because it awaits him as he stands on its brink, or as a description of his afterlife state.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p226#5/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p226#5/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p226#5/r2.claim: The clause about being given drink coordinates with an omitted phrase about what he will encounter in Hell; ṣadīd is the pus flowing from the skin of Hell's inhabitants and clarifies the vague word water.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p418#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p418#2/r1.speaker: أبو عبيدة والأزهري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p418#2/r1.claim: They treat waraʾ as a word with opposite senses, meaning either before or behind.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p418#2/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p418#2/r10.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة والضحاك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p418#2/r10.claim: They identify ṣadīd as fluid running from the bodies of Hell's inhabitants.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p418#2/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p418#2/r11.speaker: محمد بن كعب والربيع
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p418#2/r11.claim: They identify it as the washings of Hell's inhabitants in Hell.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p418#2/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p418#2/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p418#2/r12.claim: Another report says it is fluid running from the private parts of adulterers, male and female.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p418#2/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p418#2/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p418#2/r13.claim: A lexical explanation derives ṣadīd from turning away: it is repellent pus from which people recoil.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p418#2/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p418#2/r14.speaker: أبو أمامة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p418#2/r14.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet says the drink is brought near reluctantly; it burns the face and scalp, then cuts the intestines until they exit the drinker's rear. No grading is stated.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p418#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p418#2/r2.speaker: ثعلب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p418#2/r2.claim: Waraʾ names whatever is concealed from someone, whether it lies ahead or behind.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p418#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p418#2/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p418#2/r3.claim: Another explanation takes waraʾ as behind the person, in pursuit, or as something that will come later.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p418#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p418#2/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p418#2/r4.claim: Yusqā can coordinate with an omitted verb, ‘he is cast into it,’ or with the governing element of min warāʾihi, functioning as a descriptive clause.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p418#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p418#2/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p418#2/r5.claim: Hell is parsed as the subject of the passive verb; the apparent sense is that the drink is real water.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p418#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p418#2/r6.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p418#2/r6.claim: He treats ṣadīd as an adjective of water, while explaining that it is not literally water but is called water by customary usage as its substitute.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p418#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p418#2/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p418#2/r7.claim: An alternative supplies an omitted comparison: it is like pus, rather than pus itself.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p418#2/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p418#2/r8.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p418#2/r8.claim: He analyzes ṣadīd as explanatory apposition to the indefinite māʾ; Abū Ḥayyān notes Basran grammarians reject such apposition with indefinites, unlike Kufans and al-Fārisī.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p418#2/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p418#2/r9.speaker: الحوفي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p418#2/r9.claim: He parses ṣadīd as an adjective qualifying water.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p418/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p418/r6.speaker: أبو عبيدة وابن الأنباري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p418/r6.claim: Abu Ubayda and Ibn al-Anbari interpret min warāʾihi as ‘after him’; a poem says no one can flee from God.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p418/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p418/r7.speaker: أبو عبيدة وقطرب والطبري والزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p418/r7.claim: Other authorities take min warāʾihi as ‘in front of him’; the author relates this to Hell awaiting him in worldly life or at resurrection.

SAMIN-DURR:14:16#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:14:16#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:14:16#2/r1.claim: One parse makes صديد an adjective of ماء, either by omitted comparison (water like pus) or by calling resembling pus “water”; Ibn Atiyya takes the latter.

SAMIN-DURR:14:16#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:14:16#2/r2.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:14:16#2/r2.claim: Ibn Atiyya says the drink is actual pus called water for its resemblance to water.

SAMIN-DURR:14:16#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:14:16#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:14:16#2/r3.claim: The adjective is awkward because صديد is not derived, unless explained as مصدود, something avoided due to disgust.

SAMIN-DURR:14:16#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:14:16#2/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:14:16#2/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhshari parses صديد as apposition; Basrans disallow this among indefinite nouns, unlike Kufans and al-Farisi.

SAMIN-DURR:14:16#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:14:16#2/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:14:16#2/r5.claim: A third grammatical parse makes صديد a بدل.

SAMIN-DURR:14:16#2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:14:16#2/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:14:16#2/r6.claim: صديد is fluid from Hell-dwellers' bodies, or pus between skin and flesh.

SAMIN-DURR:14:16/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:14:16/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:14:16/r1.claim: من ورائه جهنم may be a genitive adjectival clause for جبار, or the prepositional phrase alone may be the adjective with جهنم as subject.

SAMIN-DURR:14:16/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:14:16/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:14:16/r2.claim: ويسقى may coordinate with the previous adjective; alternatively it coordinates with an omitted يلقى فيها.

SAMIN-DURR:14:16/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:14:16/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:14:16/r3.claim: وراء normally means behind; a contrary sense “in front” is attributed to Abu Ubayda, Qutrub, and Ibn Jarir, with poetry as evidence.

SAMIN-DURR:14:16/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:14:16/r4.speaker: ثعلب
SAMIN-DURR:14:16/r4.claim: Thaalab says وراء is what is hidden from sight, whether behind or ahead.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p484#3/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p484#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p484#3/r1.claim: Here wara means what lies ahead: Hell waits for the obstinate tyrant, who remains there forever and is shown it morning and evening until Judgment Day; Ibn Abbas read 18:79 as 'a king in front of them'.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p484#3/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p484#3/r2.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p484#3/r2.claim: Mujahid and Ikrima define sadeed as pus and blood; Qatada says it is what flows from the skin and flesh, or the contents of a disbeliever's body mixed with pus and blood.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p484#3/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p484#3/r3.speaker: أسماء بنت يزيد بن السكن
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p484#3/r3.claim: In a report from Asma bint Yazid, the Prophet defines the clay of khabal as the pus—or, in another wording, the extract—of Hell's inhabitants.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p484#3/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p484#3/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p484#3/r4.claim: Abu Umama's report says the drink burns the face and scalp when brought near and cuts the drinker's bowels until they exit; it cites 47:15 and 18:29.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p484#3/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p484#3/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p484#3/r5.claim: The drink is either boiling water at the extreme of heat or ghassaq at the extreme of cold and foulness.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p178/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p178/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p178/r3.claim: Hell lies ahead of the arrogant denier as his unavoidable destination, and ṣadīd is the discharge of the people of Hell, including pus and blood.

DURR-FULL:v5p14#2/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p14#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p14#2/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says ṣadīd is fluid that runs between the disbeliever's skin and flesh.

DURR-FULL:v5p14#2/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p14#2/r5.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v5p14#2/r5.claim: Ikrima identifies ṣadīd as pus and blood.

DURR-FULL:v5p14#2/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p14#2/r6.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v5p14#2/r6.claim: Mujahid also glosses ṣadīd as blood and pus; Qatadah describes it as fluid running between flesh and skin.

DURR-FULL:v5p14#2/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p14#2/r7.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v5p14#2/r7.claim: Hasan says that if a bucket of Hell's pus were lowered from the sky, its smell would ruin life for the people of earth.

ALUSI-FULL:v13p201#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p201#2/r1.speaker: الزجاج والطبري وقطرب وجماعة
ALUSI-FULL:v13p201#2/r1.claim: They read وراء as before or in front of the person, since the condemned person is stationed at Hell's brink and headed toward it.

ALUSI-FULL:v13p201#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p201#2/r10.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v13p201#2/r10.claim: Al-Zamakhshari parses ṣadīd as an explanatory apposition to ماء; the initial vagueness followed by specification heightens the horror.

ALUSI-FULL:v13p201#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p201#2/r11.speaker: الكوفيون والفارسي
ALUSI-FULL:v13p201#2/r11.claim: The Kufans and al-Farisi allow explanatory apposition with indefinite nouns; Basran grammarians reject that parse.

ALUSI-FULL:v13p201#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p201#2/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p201#2/r12.claim: On the Basran analysis, ṣadīd is either an appositive noun or an adjective meaning that this water prevents drinking because of its foulness.

ALUSI-FULL:v13p201#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p201#2/r13.speaker: الحوفي وابن عطية
ALUSI-FULL:v13p201#2/r13.claim: Al-Hawfi and Ibn Atiyya take ṣadīd as an adjective, comparing the construction to calling a ring iron.

ALUSI-FULL:v13p201#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p201#2/r14.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v13p201#2/r14.claim: Another adjectival analysis supplies an implicit comparison: the drink is water like ṣadīd.

ALUSI-FULL:v13p201#2/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p201#2/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p201#2/r15.claim: Mentioning this particular drink among Hell's punishments signals that it is one of the severest kinds.

ALUSI-FULL:v13p201#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p201#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p201#2/r2.claim: On the frontward reading, Hell is ahead of the condemned, who stands at its edge and is destined to enter it.

ALUSI-FULL:v13p201#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p201#2/r3.speaker: ابن الأنباري
ALUSI-FULL:v13p201#2/r3.claim: Ibn al-Anbari takes وراء to mean behind, after one's life, as in the cited verse about having no refuge beyond God.

ALUSI-FULL:v13p201#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p201#2/r4.speaker: أبو عبيدة والأزهري
ALUSI-FULL:v13p201#2/r4.claim: They treat وراء as a lexical opposite, usable for both what is in front and what is behind.

ALUSI-FULL:v13p201#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p201#2/r5.speaker: جماعة
ALUSI-FULL:v13p201#2/r5.claim: Another group calls وراء a shared semantic term for what is hidden from someone, covering both front and back; it can figuratively mean future time.

ALUSI-FULL:v13p201#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p201#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p201#2/r6.claim: The phrase about being given drink is most often parsed as answering an implicit question about what happens next, though attachment to an omitted complement is also possible.

ALUSI-FULL:v13p201#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p201#2/r7.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة والضحاك
ALUSI-FULL:v13p201#2/r7.claim: They identify ṣadīd as fluid that runs from the bodies of Hell's inhabitants.

ALUSI-FULL:v13p201#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p201#2/r8.speaker: محمد بن كعب والربيع
ALUSI-FULL:v13p201#2/r8.claim: They identify ṣadīd as fluid running from the genitals of adulterous men and women.

ALUSI-FULL:v13p201#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p201#2/r9.speaker: عكرمة
ALUSI-FULL:v13p201#2/r9.claim: Ikrima explains ṣadīd as blood and pus.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p210/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p210/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p210/r1.claim: من ورائه جهنم modifies “stubborn tyrant”: his worldly failure is not his full punishment, since Hell awaits him after death; وراء metaphorically means what comes later and may be unseen, as in Q 18:79.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p210/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p210/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p210/r2.claim: Hudbah ibn Khashram's verse uses وراء for a near relief following hardship; Ibn ʿĀshūr says the sense “after” is related but a distinct usage.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p210/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p210/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p210/r3.claim: صديد is pus-like fluid from a boil; calling it water is an emphatic metaphor because water is what one drinks, and it replaces water if the damned seek a drink.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p210/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p210/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p210/r4.claim: Making صديد an appositive to ماء is one form of emphatic metaphor; drinking pus is an added punishment beyond Hell's fire.

TABATABAI:14:15-18/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:15-18/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:15-18/r6.claim: Ṣadīd is liquid pus from a wound; tarajjuʿ means swallowing repeatedly sip by sip, and isāgha means letting a drink pass easily through the throat.

ASAD-NOTES:14:13#n22/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:14:13#n22/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:14:13#n22/r1.claim: Sadid derives from aversion and can denote repulsive matter such as pus or corpse-fluid; Asad renders the drink as bitter distress, a metaphor for afterlife suffering and frustration.

ASAD-NOTES:14:13#n22/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:14:13#n22/r2.speaker: Razi
ASAD-NOTES:14:13#n22/r2.claim: Razi reads ma' sadid as purely metaphorical, meaning water like what is called sadid.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Verses 5–17 present Moses and other messengers facing hardship, persevering, and ultimately prevailing; the Prophet and companions should persist first and show gratitude in the final phase.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The section is generally phrased but addresses Muslims, assuring them that messengers endured severe hardship, even exile, yet believers ultimately succeed.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The verses describe the afterlife punishment awaiting the rebellious.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:15/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:15/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:15/r1.claim: When opponents denied religious freedom and tried to force prophets back to their religion, the prophets sought God’s help and victory; God aided them and destroyed the arrogant tyrants, while Hell still awaits those rulers with the punishments described.

STUDYQURAN:14:16/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:14:16/r2.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:14:16/r2.claim: Beyond him lies Hell means that after death the tyrant will go to Hell.

STUDYQURAN:14:16/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:14:16/r3.speaker: Q, Z
STUDYQURAN:14:16/r3.claim: An alternate reading is that Hell lies before him in this life, as if he stands at its edge about to fall in.

STUDYQURAN:14:16/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:14:16/r4.speaker: Bg, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:14:16/r4.claim: The oozing pus is a mixture of blood and pus.

STUDYQURAN:14:16/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:14:16/r5.speaker: Bg, Z
STUDYQURAN:14:16/r5.claim: The pus oozes from the bodies of Hell's people.

STUDYQURAN:14:intro/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:14:intro/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:14:intro/r7.claim: Another theme is the terrible nature of divine chastisement in this world and the next.
